section_summary: This section covers United States and Allied policy regarding taxation in occupied Japan between 1946 and 1949, focusing on extraordinary taxes, the taxation of foreign nationals, and tax treaty considerations. Major topics include Far Eastern Commission consultations with SCAP concerning extraordinary Japanese taxation and Allied safeguards, Department of State legal analyses regarding the feasibility of concluding a bilateral double taxation convention with Japan prior to a general peace treaty, and the preliminary recommendations of the Shoup Tax Mission. Additionally, the records document petitions against Japanese tax reassessments and legislative proposals sponsored by the American Chamber of Commerce in Japan and Allied trade bodies seeking income tax deductions for foreign businessmen to encourage foreign investment and economic recovery.

subfiles.about: Transmittal of the Far Eastern Commission's request for consultation with SCAP regarding Japanese extraordinary taxation laws and safeguards for Allied nationals, accompanied by an informal communication from SCAP.
subfiles.from: Frank R. McCoy, Chairman, Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.summary: FEC Chairman Frank R. McCoy transmits a unanimously adopted request for consultation with SCAP regarding extraordinary Japanese tax legislation and safeguards for United Nations nationals. The transmission includes a certified copy of the consultation resolution and an informal communication from SCAP detailing Japan's capital levy and 100 percent tax on war indemnity claims.
subfiles.title: Letter Transmitting Far Eastern Commission Request for Consultation with SCAP Relative to Extraordinary Taxation in Japan, with Enclosures
subfiles.to: Dean Acheson, Acting Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Duplicate copy of the Far Eastern Commission Chairman's transmittal letter and enclosed consultation request regarding extraordinary Japanese taxation affecting Allied interests.
subfiles.from: Frank R. McCoy, Chairman, Far Eastern Commission
subfiles.summary: Duplicate copy of FEC Chairman Frank R. McCoy's letter transmitting the Commission's consultation request regarding extraordinary taxation in Japan and safeguards for Allied nationals.
subfiles.title: Duplicate Copy of Letter Transmitting Request for Consultation with SCAP Relative to Extraordinary Taxation in Japan, with Enclosure
subfiles.to: Dean Acheson, Acting Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Request to forward the Far Eastern Commission's consultation message and press release instructions concerning Japanese extraordinary taxation to the Joint Chiefs of Staff for transmission to SCAP.
subfiles.from: J. H. Hilldring, State Department Member, State-War-Navy Coordinating Committee
subfiles.summary: SWNCC Member J. H. Hilldring requests that the Secretary of State forward the Far Eastern Commission's consultative message on extraordinary Japanese taxation to the Joint Chiefs of Staff for transmission to SCAP.
subfiles.title: Memorandum on Consultation with the Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers Relative to Extraordinary Taxation in Japan, with Enclosure

subfiles.about: An inquiry to SCAP regarding whether non-yen income determines the tax bracket for yen income of foreign nationals under Japanese income tax law and SCAPIN 4938-A.
subfiles.summary: The State Department requests SCAP clarify whether foreign nationals' non-yen income affects their yen income tax brackets under Japanese law and SCAPIN 4938-A.
subfiles.title: Inquiry Regarding Japanese Income Taxation of Foreign Nationals
subfiles.to: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers, Tokyo

subfiles.about: SCAP's reply clarifying that only yen income determines the income tax bracket rates for foreign nationals under Japanese law and SCAPIN 4938-A.
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: SCAP informs the State Department that only yen income determines income tax brackets for foreign nationals under Japanese law and SCAPIN 4938-A.
subfiles.title: Clarification on Income Tax Bracket Determination for Foreign Nationals in Japan

subfiles.about: An inquiry asking whether an international convention for the avoidance of double taxation can be concluded with Japan before a peace treaty is signed.
subfiles.from: Mitchell B. Carroll, Special Counsel, Tax Committee, National Foreign Trade Council
subfiles.summary: Mitchell B. Carroll of the National Foreign Trade Council inquires whether a double taxation convention can be concluded with Japan before a peace treaty.
subfiles.title: Inquiry Regarding Possibility of Concluding a Double Taxation Convention with Japan
subfiles.to: Dean Acheson, Secretary of State (Attention: Frederick Livesey)

subfiles.about: Internal transmittal referring the double taxation inquiry to the Treaty Branch, agreeing that the earlier August 25 draft reply should not be sent.
subfiles.from: G. Strong, Division of Financial Affairs (OFD:FN)
subfiles.summary: OFD refers the Japan tax convention inquiry to L/T, agreeing the August 25 draft reply should not be sent.
subfiles.title: Referral of Inquiry Regarding Proposed Tax Convention with Japan
subfiles.to: W. V. Whittington, Treaty Branch, Office of the Legal Adviser (L/T)

subfiles.about: Official State Department publication containing the texts of the Declaration by United Nations of January 1, 1942 and the Atlantic Charter of August 14, 1941.
subfiles.summary: This State Department publication contains the Declaration by United Nations of January 1, 1942, pledging full cooperation against the Axis and prohibiting separate armistices or peace treaties. It also reproduces the Atlantic Charter of August 14, 1941, setting forth common principles for postwar peace, security, and economic collaboration.
subfiles.title: Executive Agreement Series 236: Cooperative War Effort (Declaration by United Nations and Atlantic Charter)

subfiles.about: An unapproved draft reply proposing to defer discussing a tax convention with Japan until Dr. Carl Shoup returns with his mission's report.
subfiles.from: Frederick Livesey, Adviser, Office of Financial and Development Policy
subfiles.summary: Draft letter to Carroll suggesting deferral of discussions on a bilateral tax convention until Dr. Carl Shoup returns with his mission's report.
subfiles.title: Draft Reply to National Foreign Trade Council Regarding Tax Convention with Japan
subfiles.to: Mitchell B. Carroll, Special Counsel, Tax Committee, National Foreign Trade Council

subfiles.about: A note proposing to add the phrase "prior to the consummation of a Treaty of Peace" to the draft reply to Carroll.
subfiles.summary: Snow suggests adding 'prior to the consummation of a Treaty of Peace' to the draft reply.
subfiles.title: Suggested Amendment to Proposed Reply on Japanese Tax Convention
subfiles.to: Frederick Livesey, Office of Financial and Development Policy (OFD)

subfiles.about: Legal analysis concluding that while international law does not strictly forbid concluding a tax treaty with occupied Japan, policy considerations make it highly unlikely.
subfiles.from: W. V. Whittington, Treaty Branch, Office of the Legal Adviser (L/T)
subfiles.summary: L/T examines international law on occupied Japan's treaty-making capacity, advising that while theoretically possible, concluding a bilateral tax convention is impractical and might imply a separate peace contrary to United Nations commitments.
subfiles.title: Legal Memorandum: Possibility of Concluding a Tax Convention with Japan
subfiles.to: Frederick Livesey, Office of Financial and Development Policy (OFD) (through C. E. Snow, L/P)

subfiles.about: Memorandum criticizing the August 25 draft reply, opposing a tax treaty with Japan ahead of Latin American nations, and requesting legal guidance.
subfiles.from: Frederick Livesey, Office of Financial and Development Policy (OFD)
subfiles.summary: Livesey objects to the earlier draft reply, opposes prioritizing a Japanese tax treaty over Latin American negotiations, and seeks legal guidance regarding the state of war.
subfiles.title: Office Memorandum: Is It Possible to Negotiate a Tax Treaty with Japan Before a Peace Treaty
subfiles.to: Mr. Doherty, Division of Financial Affairs (FN)

subfiles.about: Official reply stating that concluding a tax convention with Japan prior to a peace treaty is highly unlikely under existing circumstances.
subfiles.from: Frederick Livesey, Adviser, Office of Financial and Development Policy (for the Secretary of State)
subfiles.summary: Livesey informs Carroll that concluding a tax convention with Japan prior to a peace treaty is highly unlikely under existing circumstances.
subfiles.title: Reply to National Foreign Trade Council Concerning Tax Convention with Japan
subfiles.to: Mitchell B. Carroll, Special Counsel, Tax Committee, National Foreign Trade Council

subfiles.about: A report by Dr. Carl Shoup communicating tentative recommendations of the tax mission for comprehensive reform of the Japanese tax system.
subfiles.from: Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers, Tokyo (from Carl Shoup for West)
subfiles.summary: Dr. Carl Shoup transmits the tentative recommendations of his tax mission, including repeal of the excess profits tax, personal income tax reforms, revaluation of corporate assets, and administrative improvements.
subfiles.title: Preliminary Recommendations of the Shoup Tax Mission to Japan

subfiles.about: An appeal by a former Chinese resident of Osaka against repeated and excessive income tax reassessments imposed by Japanese authorities after his business failed.
subfiles.summary: San Ki So petitions the Far East Committee against repeated and excessive income tax reassessments imposed by the Osaka Revenue Bureau following the collapse of his business.
subfiles.title: Petition Regarding Improper Re-taxation by Japanese Tax Officials
subfiles.to: Far East Committee in Washington D.C.

subfiles.about: Transmittal of recommendations and draft legislation from the American Chamber of Commerce in Japan proposing a tax deduction of up to 2,000,000 yen for foreign businessmen.
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo (C. H. Boehringer)
keywords: American Chamber of Commerce in Japan
subfiles.summary: USPOLAD Tokyo transmits an American Chamber of Commerce memorandum and draft bill proposing foreign businessmen receive an income tax deduction up to 2,000,000 yen for living expenses to encourage foreign investment.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 741: Suggestions Concerning Taxation of Foreign Nationals Prepared by American Chamber of Commerce in Japan, with Enclosures

subfiles.about: Transmittal of revised joint proposals from American, British, and Dutch trade bodies requesting a 70 percent living expense tax deduction for foreign nationals, with comments from GHQ tax officials.
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo (C. H. Boehringer)
keywords: American Chamber of Commerce in Japan
subfiles.summary: USPOLAD Tokyo transmits revised joint proposals by American, British, and Dutch trade associations requesting a Japanese income tax deduction of up to seventy percent of gross income for foreign businessmen's necessary living expenses. The despatch includes their joint letter to Finance Minister Hayato Ikeda and revised draft legislation, explaining that high taxes and living costs severely hinder foreign commerce. It also reports that Deputy Chief Henry Shavell of GHQ's Internal Revenue Division expressed willingness to give sympathetic consideration to a mutually agreeable tax exemption plan.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 803: Revised Suggestions Concerning Taxation of Foreign Nationals in Japan, with Enclosures

subfiles.about: An airgram reporting a SCAP press release regarding increased Japanese judicial penalties and fines against tax evaders and black-marketeers.
subfiles.from: United States Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo (W. Diehl)
subfiles.summary: USPOLAD Tokyo reports a SCAP press release detailing sharp increases in Japanese court fines and property confiscations against tax evaders and black-market violators.
subfiles.title: Airgram A-349: SCAP Press Release on Japanese Courts Dealing Severely with Tax and Economic Violators
